<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par129 />be regarded as a transposition, but {{GHGheb|text=מִזְמוֹר}} is used epexegetically for the general term omitted before {{GHGheb|text=לְדָוִד}} (as it were, a poem ''of David, a psalm''). Moreover, the introduction of the author, poet, &c., by this ''Lamed auctoris'' is the customary idiom also in the other Semitic dialects, especially in Arabic.

{{GHGmargin-letter|129|d}}
(''b'') When a genitive is to be made dependent on a nomen regens, which is itself composed of a nomen regens and rectum, and represents, as a compound, one united idea, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=חֶלְקַת הַשָּׁדֶה לְבֹעַז|translate=the portion of field belonging to Boaz}} ({{GHGheb|text=חֶ׳ שְׂדֵה בֹעַז}} would be ''the portion of the field of Boaz''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=9}} ''at the house-door of Elisha''. This especially applies to the cases in which the compound regens represents a term in very common use, the fixed form of which cannot be altered, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=עַל־סֵ֫פֶר דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים לְמַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל|translate=in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel}}; 15:23, &c.; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=19|verse=51}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|129|e}}
(''c'') When for any other reason the construction with the nomen regens in the construct state is inadmissible; cf. e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=18|verse=20}}, where {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכָבְתְּךָ}}, on account of the suffix, cannot be used in the construct state; but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=15|verse=16}} ff., &c., {{GHGheb|text=שִׁכְבַת־זֶ֫רַע}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=3|verse=28}} ''the Jordan fords of Moab'' ({{GHGheb|text=יַרְדֵּן}} as a ''proper name'' cannot be used in the construct state); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=5}} ''upon the third and upon the fourth generation of them that hate me''; {{GHGheb|text=וְעַל־רִבֵּעִים}} must be kept in the absolute state for the sake of conformity with {{GHGheb|text=עַל־שִׁלֵּשִׁים}}, and for the same reason also {{GHGheb|text=לַֽאֲלָפִים לְאֹֽהֲבַי}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|129|f}}
(''d'') After statements of number in such cases as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּשִׁבְעָה וְעֶשְׂרִים יוֹם לַחֹ֫דֶשׁ|translate=on the seven and twentieth day of the month}}; cf. 7:11, 16:3 and frequently, or as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=1|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּשְׁנַת שְׁתַּ֫יִם לְדָֽרְיָ֫וֶשׁ|translate=in the second year of Darius}}; the numeral here is always one compound idea with the substantive numbered, and consequently (as in the examples under ''b'') does not admit of being in the constr. st. with a genitive. The same naturally applies also to such examples as {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=3|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי לְלִדְתִּי|translate=on the third day of my giving birth}} (i.e. after my giving birth). Cf. also the standing phrase {{GHGheb|text=בְּאֶחָד לַחֹ֫דֶשׁ|translate=on the first}} (day) ''of the month'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=5}} and frequently.

{{GHGmargin-letter|129|g}}
Rem. In cases like {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=2}} ''and his firstborn was Amnon'' {{GHGheb|text=לַֽאֲחִינֹ֫עַם|translate=of Ahinoam}}, the genitive expressed by circumlocution with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} is in reality dependent on a regens which is omitted ({{GHGheb|text=בֵּן לַֽאֲחִינֹ֫עַם|translate=a son of Ahinoam}}); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=3}}, 5, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=3}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=לְבֵית יִשְׂרָאֵל}} originally depended on ''thus spake the Lord''), and the remarks on {{GHGheb|text=לְדָוִד מִזְמוֹר}} under ''c'' above.

{{GHGmargin-letter|129|h}}
2. The periphrastic expression of the genitive by means of {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר לְ}} is used principally to state the ''possessor'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=הַצֹּאן אֲשֶׁר לְאָבִ֫יהָ}} ''her father’s sheep'' (prop. ''the sheep which'' belonged ''to her father''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=4}} and frequently. So also (according to {{GHGpar|128|a}}) when a genitive depends on more than one substantive, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=5}} ''the butler and the baker who'' (belonged) ''to the king of Egypt'' ({{GHGheb|text=וְאֹפֵה מֶ֫לֶךְ מִצְרַ֫יִם}} would indicate only the baker as belonging to the king); or when a genitive (as in the examples under ''d'' above) is added to a compound, which expresses one united idea ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=4|verse=3}}); or when, as a fixed term (e.g. a title), it appears always in the same form, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים אֲשֶׁר לִשְׁלֹמֹה|translate=the Song of songs, of Solomon}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=11|verse=10}}; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=43}}.<ref>In New Hebrew {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁל}} (derived from {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁלְּ}} = {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר לְ}}, see § 36, and cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=3|verse=7|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁלִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁלִּשְׁלֹמֹה}}) is used like the simple relative {{GHGheb|text=דִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=דְּ}} in Aramaic, as an independent sign of the genitive.</ref><section end=par129 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
